tables.name: budget_lines
tables.description: Federal budget line items from the Budget in Brief documents, FY2009-10 → FY2026-27.
tables.notes: Rs million. Each printed row carried 1–4 numeric columns; is_own_year_be = TRUE marks the document's own-year Budget Estimate, which is the only column safe to string into a time series. The low-numbered 'Budget at a Glance' tables extract noisily and item wording drifts between years — match with ILIKE and sanity-check.

tables.name: district_indicators
tables.description: Every district-level indicator in Data Darbar, one row per district × indicator × year.
tables.notes: Long format so heterogeneous sources share one table. Filter `kind = 'indicator'` for the measures themselves; kind='quality' rows carry the sample size and small-n flag for the same prefix, and kind='provenance' rows record borrowed estimates. Survey groups suppress cells with n<30 upstream, so an absent row can mean 'suppressed' as well as 'not collected'. DOUBLE-COUNTING TRAP: where a district was split after Census 2017 (see the *_boundary_change provenance rows) both halves carry the SAME 2017 figure for the combined pre-split area, so summing a 2017 count across all districts overstates the total. Filter those rows out, or sum the 2023 year instead.

tables.name: mouza_crosswalk
tables.description: Maps each PBS tehsil to the ADM3 polygon Data Darbar maps it on.
tables.notes: MANY-TO-ONE by design: PBS enumerates 595 tehsils against the boundary file's 553, because it carries sub-tehsils created after the polygons were drawn. Since every Mouza Census figure is a count of mouzas, summing several PBS tehsils into one polygon is the correct operation — group by tehsil_id and sum before taking any share. match records how each row was resolved: exact_name, variant (same place spelled differently), contained, fuzzy, only_tehsil_in_district, parent (a sub-tehsil folded into the unit it was carved from), and approx (no polygon exists for the area, so it was placed in a neighbour — treat those tehsils' placement as a judgement call). All 48,738 mouzas are assigned. The 10 unresolved rows all have zero mouzas.
tables.source: PBS Mouza Census 2020 frame × geoBoundaries PAK ADM3

tables.name: mouza_tehsil
tables.description: Mouza Census 2020 facility counts, one row per PBS tehsil.
tables.notes: Every column is a COUNT OF MOUZAS (revenue villages), never of people or households — a mouza of 12,000 and a mouza of 300 each count once. PBS publishes numerators without a denominator, and its own indicator blocks disagree about how many mouzas answered: only 33 of the 544 enumerated tehsils give a single consistent base, and blocks can differ by up to 181. Take each block's own row sum as its base rather than TotalMauzaCount. Existance/NotExistance pairs are exclusive; drinking water, health facility type, fuel, street surface and media are multiple response, so they can sum past the base. The frame is rural — cities are not revenue villages — but mouzas that urbanise stay in it (4.9% urban, 2.4% partly urban). 51 tehsils return all zeros: AJK and GB were not enumerated, nor were Mand and Tump in Kech or Kallag in Panjgur. Join to the ADM3 geography through mouza_crosswalk. Column names keep PBS's own casing and spelling; DuckDB matches them case-insensitively.

tables.name: sbp_observations
tables.description: The macro time-series panel: every observation of every SBP series held here.
tables.notes: One row per series × date. UNITS ARE PER-SERIES — join to sbp_series_catalog and read `unit` before summing anything, because this table mixes rupees, dollars, percentages and index levels in one `value` column. value IS NULL where SBP suppressed or has not published the figure and `status` says which ('Normal', 'Missing value', …) — a NULL is not a zero. Frequencies are mixed, so filter on the catalogue's `frequency` before resampling or averaging across series. DOUBLE-COUNTING TRAP (country-wise remittances, TS_GP_BOP_WR_M): the country series are hierarchical, so summing them all overstates the total by ~42% (FY2024-25: 54,384 vs the published 38,299 Mn USD). 'U.A.E.' already contains Dubai, Abu Dhabi, Sharjah and 'Other four U.A.E.'s States'; 'Other GCC Countries excluding Saudi Arabia & U.A.E.' already contains Bahrain, Kuwait, Oman and Qatar; 'ten European Countries' already contains Belgium, Denmark, France, Germany, Greece, Ireland, Italy, Netherland, Spain and Sweden — Norway and Switzerland are reported separately. The partition that reconciles exactly to the published total is: Saudi Arabia, U.A.E., U.K., U.S.A., Other GCC, ten European Countries, Norway, Switzerland, Australia, Canada, Japan, Malaysia, South Africa, South Korea, Other Countries. The same shape applies to province-wise banking (TS_GP_BAM_ADVDEP_HY), where 'all Pakistan' is the total of the regional series.
tables.source: State Bank of Pakistan, EasyData API (easydata.sbp.org.pk)

tables.name: sbp_series_catalog
tables.description: Every SBP EasyData series held here: name, unit, frequency, coverage, method note.
tables.notes: One row per series — browse this first, then join to sbp_observations on series_key. DATE CONVENTION: observations are stamped on the LAST day of their period, and annual series on the last day of the FISCAL year, so FY2023-24 appears as 2024-06-30. Not every annual series is fiscal though — population and literacy are calendar years. `available_upto` is SBP's own claim and several datasets are stale (province-wise banking stops at Jun-2023), so check it before presenting a series as current.

examples.title: Ten poorest districts
examples.sql:
SELECT rank, name, prov, mpi, H, A
FROM mpi_districts
WHERE low_n = 0
ORDER BY rank
LIMIT 10;

examples.title: Female literacy, 2017 vs 2023
examples.sql:
SELECT district, province,
       max(value) FILTER (year = '2017') AS lit_2017,
       max(value) FILTER (year = '2023') AS lit_2023,
       round(max(value) FILTER (year = '2023')
           - max(value) FILTER (year = '2017'), 1) AS change
FROM district_indicators
WHERE indicator = 'literacy_ratio_female'
GROUP BY 1, 2
ORDER BY change DESC;

examples.title: Top import partners, FY2024-25 (Rs bn)
examples.sql:
SELECT country, round(sum(fy_value_kpkr) / 1e6, 1) AS rs_bn
FROM trade_hs8
WHERE direction = 'import' AND fiscal_year = '2024-25'
  AND country IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY rs_bn DESC
LIMIT 15;

examples.title: What Pakistan exports most (FY2024-25)
examples.sql:
SELECT hs8, any_value(commodity) AS commodity,
       round(sum(fy_value_kpkr) / 1e6, 1) AS rs_bn
FROM trade_hs8
WHERE direction = 'export' AND fiscal_year = '2024-25'
  AND country IS NULL
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY rs_bn DESC
LIMIT 20;

examples.title: Real GDP growth by year
examples.sql:
SELECT year, round(value, 2) AS growth_pct
FROM national_accounts
WHERE table_sheet = 'Table 6' AND item LIKE 'D GDP%'
ORDER BY year;

examples.title: Federal defence budget over time
examples.sql:
SELECT doc_fy, item, value_rs_mn
FROM budget_lines
WHERE is_own_year_be AND item ILIKE '%defence%'
ORDER BY doc_fy;

examples.title: Do lights track wealth? (tehsils, by province)
examples.sql:
-- Note: Meta's RWI uses night-lights as an input, so this correlation
-- is partly mechanical. Read it as consistency, not as validation.
SELECT prov,
       count(*) AS tehsils,
       round(corr(rwi, ln(nl_latest + 0.01)), 3) AS corr_rwi_lognl
FROM tehsil_satellite
WHERE nl_lowc = 0
GROUP BY 1
HAVING count(*) >= 5
ORDER BY 3 DESC;

examples.title: Night-lights, tehsil trajectories since 2020
examples.sql:
SELECT s.name AS tehsil, s.prov,
       max(l.radiance) FILTER (l.year = 2020) AS y2020,
       max(l.radiance) FILTER (l.year = 2026) AS y2026,
       s.pop
FROM tehsil_nightlights l
JOIN tehsil_satellite s USING (tehsil_id)
WHERE s.nl_lowc = 0 AND s.pop > 200000
GROUP BY 1, 2, 5
ORDER BY y2026 / nullif(y2020, 0) DESC
LIMIT 20;

examples.title: Rural electrification, worst tehsils (Mouza Census)
examples.sql:
-- Shares are of MOUZAS, not people. Aggregate to the polygon first:
-- several PBS tehsils can share one boundary.
SELECT x.dd_name AS tehsil, m.province,
       sum(m."ElectrictiyAvailability_NoneMouzas") AS no_electricity,
       sum(m."ElectrictiyAvailability_AllMouzas"
         + m."ElectrictiyAvailability_MostlyMouzas"
         + m."ElectrictiyAvailability_SomeMouzas"
         + m."ElectrictiyAvailability_NoneMouzas") AS base,
       round(100.0 * sum(m."ElectrictiyAvailability_NoneMouzas")
             / nullif(sum(m."ElectrictiyAvailability_AllMouzas"
               + m."ElectrictiyAvailability_MostlyMouzas"
               + m."ElectrictiyAvailability_SomeMouzas"
               + m."ElectrictiyAvailability_NoneMouzas"), 0), 1) AS pct_dark
FROM mouza_tehsil m
JOIN mouza_crosswalk x USING (tehsil_code)
WHERE m.TotalMauzaCount > 0
GROUP BY 1, 2 HAVING base >= 50
ORDER BY pct_dark DESC LIMIT 20;

examples.title: Do brighter tehsils have more girls' schools?
examples.sql:
-- Facilities are places, lights are satellite: this asks whether the
-- two agree, not whether either causes the other.
SELECT s.prov,
       count(*) AS tehsils,
       round(corr(g.pct_girls_primary, ln(s.nl_latest + 0.01)), 3) AS corr
FROM (SELECT x.dd_id,
             100.0 * sum(m."EducationFacility_FemalePrimaryExistanceCount")
             / nullif(sum(m."EducationFacility_FemalePrimaryExistanceCount"
               + m."EducationFacility_FemalePrimaryNotExistanceCount"), 0)
               AS pct_girls_primary
      FROM mouza_tehsil m JOIN mouza_crosswalk x USING (tehsil_code)
      WHERE m.TotalMauzaCount > 0 GROUP BY 1) g
JOIN tehsil_satellite s ON s.tehsil_id = g.dd_id
WHERE s.nl_lowc = 0
GROUP BY 1 HAVING count(*) >= 5 ORDER BY 3;

examples.title: Urbanisation vs multidimensional poverty
examples.sql:
SELECT d.district, d.province, d.value AS pct_urban_2023, m.mpi
FROM district_indicators d
JOIN mpi_districts m USING (district_key)
WHERE d.indicator = 'urban_proportion' AND d.year = '2023'
  AND m.low_n = 0
ORDER BY m.mpi DESC;

examples.title: The rupee since 1947
examples.sql:
SELECT obs_date, value AS pkr_per_usd
FROM sbp_observations
WHERE series_key = 'TS_GP_ER_FAERPKR_M.E00220'
ORDER BY obs_date;

examples.title: The real policy rate
examples.sql:
-- The policy rate only moves when SBP meets, so it cannot be joined
-- month-to-month against CPI. ASOF JOIN carries the last rate forward.
SELECT c.obs_date,
       p.value AS policy_rate,
       c.value AS cpi_yoy,
       round(p.value - c.value, 2) AS real_rate
FROM sbp_observations c
ASOF JOIN (SELECT obs_date, value FROM sbp_observations
           WHERE series_key = 'TS_GP_IR_SIRPR_AH.SBPOL0030') p
  ON p.obs_date <= c.obs_date
WHERE c.series_key = 'TS_GP_PT_CPI_M.P00011516'
ORDER BY c.obs_date;

examples.title: Where remittances come from, FY2024-25
examples.sql:
-- The country series are hierarchical: U.A.E. contains Dubai/Abu Dhabi/Sharjah,
-- 'Other GCC' contains Bahrain/Kuwait/Oman/Qatar, and 'ten European Countries'
-- contains Belgium..Sweden. Summing all of them overstates the total by ~42%,
-- so this restricts to the partition that reconciles to the published figure.
SELECT replace(c.series_name, 'Workers'' remittances received from ', '') AS source,
       round(sum(o.value), 0) AS mn_usd
FROM sbp_observations o
JOIN sbp_series_catalog c USING (series_key)
WHERE c.dataset_code = 'TS_GP_BOP_WR_M'
  AND o.obs_date BETWEEN DATE '2024-07-01' AND DATE '2025-06-30'
  AND c.series_name LIKE '%received from%'
  AND c.series_name NOT ILIKE '%Dubai%'    AND c.series_name NOT ILIKE '%Abu Dhabi%'
  AND c.series_name NOT ILIKE '%Sharjah%'  AND c.series_name NOT ILIKE '%four U.A.E%'
  AND c.series_name NOT ILIKE '%Bahrain%'  AND c.series_name NOT ILIKE '%Kuwait%'
  AND c.series_name NOT ILIKE '%Oman%'     AND c.series_name NOT ILIKE '%Qatar%'
  AND c.series_name NOT ILIKE '%Belgium%'  AND c.series_name NOT ILIKE '%Denmark%'
  AND c.series_name NOT ILIKE '%France%'   AND c.series_name NOT ILIKE '%Germany%'
  AND c.series_name NOT ILIKE '%Greece%'   AND c.series_name NOT ILIKE '%Ireland%'
  AND c.series_name NOT ILIKE '%Italy%'    AND c.series_name NOT ILIKE '%Netherland%'
  AND c.series_name NOT ILIKE '%Spain%'    AND c.series_name NOT ILIKE '%Sweden%'
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY mn_usd DESC;

examples.title: Pakistan's fiscal balance, and whether it adds up
examples.sql:
-- Revenue - Expenditure = Fiscal Balance, and + Interest = Primary Balance.
-- Both identities hold exactly in the source data.
SELECT o.obs_date,
       round(max(o.value) FILTER (c.series_name LIKE 'Total Revenue%') / 1e6, 2) AS revenue_trn,
       round(max(o.value) FILTER (c.series_name LIKE 'Total Expenditure (%') / 1e6, 2) AS spending_trn,
       round(max(o.value) FILTER (c.series_name LIKE 'Fiscal Balance%') / 1e6, 2) AS fiscal_bal_trn,
       round(100 * max(o.value) FILTER (c.series_name LIKE 'Fiscal Balance%')
                 / max(o.value) FILTER (c.series_name LIKE 'Gross Domestic Product%'), 2) AS pct_of_gdp
FROM sbp_observations o
JOIN sbp_series_catalog c USING (series_key)
WHERE c.dataset_code = 'TS_GP_PF_SPF_Y'
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY 1;

examples.title: Reserves cover: months of imports
examples.sql:
WITH res AS (
  SELECT o.obs_date, o.value AS sbp_reserves
  FROM sbp_observations o JOIN sbp_series_catalog c USING (series_key)
  WHERE c.series_name = 'Total SBP Reserves'),
imp AS (
  SELECT o.obs_date, o.value AS goods_imports
  FROM sbp_observations o JOIN sbp_series_catalog c USING (series_key)
  WHERE c.series_name = 'Goods - Import (FOB)')
SELECT r.obs_date, round(r.sbp_reserves, 0) AS reserves_mn_usd,
       round(r.sbp_reserves / nullif(avg(i.goods_imports) OVER (
            ORDER BY r.obs_date ROWS BETWEEN 11 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW), 0), 1) AS months_cover
FROM res r JOIN imp i USING (obs_date)
ORDER BY r.obs_date DESC
LIMIT 24;

examples.title: Urban vs rural food inflation
examples.sql:
SELECT o.obs_date,
       max(o.value) FILTER (c.series_name ILIKE 'Urban Food%') AS urban_food,
       max(o.value) FILTER (c.series_name ILIKE 'Rural Food%') AS rural_food
FROM sbp_observations o
JOIN sbp_series_catalog c USING (series_key)
WHERE c.dataset_code = 'TS_GP_PT_CPI_M'
  AND c.series_name ILIKE '%Year-on-Year%'
GROUP BY 1
HAVING urban_food IS NOT NULL
ORDER BY 1;

examples.title: Bank deposits by province (stops Jun-2023)
examples.sql:
-- The only sub-national SBP data. Stops Jun-2023.
SELECT c.series_name, o.obs_date, round(o.value / 1000, 1) AS rs_bn
FROM sbp_observations o
JOIN sbp_series_catalog c USING (series_key)
WHERE c.dataset_code = 'TS_GP_BAM_ADVDEP_HY'
  AND c.series_name ILIKE 'Total Outstanding Deposits%'
  AND o.obs_date = (SELECT max(obs_date) FROM sbp_observations
                    WHERE dataset_code = 'TS_GP_BAM_ADVDEP_HY')
ORDER BY rs_bn DESC;

examples.title: What SBP series are actually current?
examples.sql:
SELECT subject_area, frequency,
       count(*) AS series,
       max(available_upto) AS latest
FROM sbp_series_catalog
GROUP BY 1, 2
ORDER BY 1, series DESC;

examples.title: SBP vs PBS: two measures of the same GDP

-- Should agree: same PBS source, different distribution channel.
SELECT n.year, n.value AS pbs_workbook,
       s.value AS sbp_easydata
FROM national_accounts n
JOIN sbp_observations s
  ON s.series_key = 'TS_GP_RLS_PAKGDP15_Y.GDP00150000'
 AND CAST(left(n.year, 4) AS INT) + 1 = year(s.obs_date)
WHERE n.table_sheet = 'Table 5' AND n.item LIKE 'D GDP%'
ORDER BY n.year;
